title: TCE per-client review verdict
description: Structured result of one Codex review of one client's TCE example file. Passed to `codex exec --output-schema` so the orchestrator can gate on findings without parsing prose.
//: NOTE: `codex exec --output-schema` uses OpenAI structured outputs in strict mode, which requires `required` to list EVERY key in `properties` at every level. There is no way to mark a field optional — a schema with a genuinely optional field is rejected with a 400 before the model runs. Fields that may have nothing to say use an empty string or empty array instead.

client.description: Client key from build/example-test-harness/clients.tsv (e.g. redis-py, lettuce-async, seredis).

file.description: Repo-relative path of the example file reviewed.

verdict.description: fail if any finding has severity high; otherwise pass.

findings.description: Actionable defects only. Empty when the file is correct — do not pad with observations about what is right.

severity.description: high = wrong on the rendered page or wrong for the reader (bad output comment, wrong API, leaked scaffolding, wrong C# flavour). medium = inconsistent with the reference or the set. low = style.

line.description: 1-indexed line in `file`. 0 when the finding is about the file as a whole.

why_it_matters.description: The concrete consequence — what a reader or maintainer sees because of this. Not a restatement of the summary.

suggested_fix.description: The minimal change that resolves it. Empty string when there is nothing useful to suggest — strict mode forbids optional fields.

not_checked.description: Anything the review could not assess (a file it could not read, an API it could not confirm). Empty array when nothing was skipped. Better to declare a gap than to guess.
